result.title: ViStep-RL: Stepwise Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Visual Agents
result.summary: Long-horizon visual agents must do more than inspect images: they must turn observations into evidence that remains usable as a task unfolds. Existing active-perception methods teach agents where and how to look, while a final-answer reward gives little structure for deciding which observations satisfy dependent subgoals or should be retained for later use. We present ViStep-RL (Visual Stepwise Reinforcement Learning), which models execution as a dependency-linked graph of evidence-bearing subgoals. A verifier tracks which subgoals are supported by valid evidence, and changes in graph potential provide a net-progress learning signal; an active memory protocol preserves evidence across turns and links retrieval to downstream use. On ViInteract, ViStep-RL reaches 60.0% strict completion with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, compared with 10.0% for the base model and 46.5% after supervised fine-tuning. Controlled studies show that incremental task-state rewards outperform cumulative rewards by 3.2 points, while active evidence writing improves strict completion by 7.75 points over automatic writing. Under a common interaction framework, the task-trained ViStep-RL policy achieves 59.5% answer accuracy, 24.0 points above the strongest of six general-purpose reference models. Held-out episodes confirm the gain at both Qwen scales, and gains extend to three external visual reasoning benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: ViStep-RL 研究长时程视觉智能体如何把观测转化为可跨轮复用的证据：将任务执行建模为带依赖关系的「证据子目标」图，用验证器判断各子目标是否被有效证据支持，并以图势能变化作为净进度奖励，配合主动记忆协议保留证据，在 ViInteract 上以 Qwen2.5-VL-7B 取得 60.0% 严格完成率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其子目标级证据验证与增量进度奖励直接对应 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选、贡献分配与停止决策，主动记忆写入/检索可供核查「保留哪些观测供后续使用」这一问题，但奖励与记忆均在显式交互轨迹上，而非 latent 推理状态。
